fig_global_distribution_density: Global density of freshwater fecal indicator bacteria observations, aggregated into hexagonal bins and shaded on a logarithmic scale. Monitoring is heavily concentrated in the United States and Europe, with sparse coverage across most of the Global South and an almost complete absence over Russia and China. Observations for India include fecal and total coliform, but exclude E. coli.
fig_sampling_frequency_mismatch: Three Wisconsin freshwater monitoring sites illustrating mismatched sampling cadences. The locator map marks a daily sampled swimming beach, a monthly regulatory river site, and a quarterly long term trend site. The accompanying panels show their Escherichia coli observations over 2022 to 2023, with 101, 19, and 17 samples respectively, demonstrating that sampling frequency rather than concentration trend distinguishes the three monitoring designs.
fig_actionability_gap: Quantifying the actionability gap across freshwater monitoring sites. The left panel shows the percentage of sites retained as the minimum observation count per site increases, with only 10.8 percent of sites having at least 100 observations and 0.7 percent having at least 500. The right panel shows the distribution of mean sampling return intervals among multi sample sites, with the near daily category highlighted; only 7.0 percent of sites achieve daily or near daily sampling while most are sampled monthly or quarterly.
fig_high_frequency_case_studies: High frequency Escherichia coli monitoring at three sites on three continents during 2023. The map locates Euclid Beach in the United States, the River Lune in the United Kingdom, and the Taruheru River in New Zealand. Each time series plots daily to near daily concentrations against the 235 colony forming units per 100 millilitres safe threshold, with a shaded safe zone. Euclid Beach remained largely safe with short lived spikes, whereas the River Lune and Taruheru River exceeded the threshold for most of the year, showing that low frequency sampling would misrepresent safety in both transient and chronic regimes.
fig_global_safety_summary: Global safety of high frequency Escherichia coli monitoring sites. The map plots sites with at least near daily sampling, coloured by the share of samples exceeding 235 colony forming units per 100 millilitres from green for consistently safe to red for chronically exceeding, showing that high frequency monitoring is almost entirely confined to North America and Europe. The donut chart summarises that across 631 sites and 235,398 samples, 77.6 percent of observations were at or below the safe threshold and 22.4 percent exceeded it.
